title: Contractor discovery · 30 minutes
opening: I’d like to understand how material purchasing works on your jobs, where it gets difficult, and what you would actually want help with. We’ll use a recent order, then agree on one useful next step.

questions.text: What projects are you running now, and what stage is each one at?
questions.hint: Project type, number of active jobs, next material package. Capture facts, not an assumed contractor profile.

questions.text: Who currently prepares material lists, chooses suppliers and places orders?
questions.hint: GC, office staff, homeowner, designer, subs or a mix. What already works well?

questions.text: Walk me through your most recent material order, from the first list to arrival on site.
questions.hint: Which material, supplier and people were involved? Ask for the sequence before naming our services.

questions.text: Which part took the most effort or did not go as expected?
questions.hint: Ask what happened, who fixed it and how. If nothing went wrong, record that too.

questions.text: Roughly how much of your time did that order take, and who did you have to contact?
questions.hint: Separate supplier, homeowner/designer and subcontractor calls. Include messages and store trips. Record an estimate or unknown; do not invent a count.

questions.text: Which one or two material packages cause the most repeated work for you?
questions.hint: Use the department selector below. Explore the relevant packages; do not interview all 17 departments in one call.

questions.text: How often does that happen, and what does it affect when it does?
questions.hint: One recent example, events per week/month, GC time, crew waiting or documented extra cost. Distinguish his estimate from verified records.

questions.text: What have you tried to make this easier, and what still falls back on you?
questions.hint: Existing supplier rep, employee, software, sub or another service. What should we preserve?

questions.text: Who should confirm quantities and specifications, approve spending, and check the delivery on site?
questions.hint: Name each role. Avantia coordinates approved purchases; the contractor/team receives and checks the materials.

questions.text: When your sub needs materials, how would you want the request and approval to reach us?
questions.hint: Direct contact or through GC; who supplies the approved list, who may approve a reorder, preferred channel and spending limit if any.

questions.text: What would you hand over, and what would you prefer to keep handling yourself?
questions.hint: Ask about supplier relationships, homeowner selections and urgent requests. Record concerns and excluded work; do not promise everything.

questions.text: If we could take only one or two recurring tasks off your plate, which would you choose?
questions.hint: Repeat his words before showing matching Avantia services. Confirm what matters most to him.

questions.text: What would make the first order feel successful enough to use us again?
questions.hint: Choose an observable result: fewer GC calls, less GC time, a complete approved order or a like-for-like price comparison. No guaranteed savings.

questions.text: Have I understood the problem and the work you want us to take over correctly?
questions.hint: Read back: problem, department, Avantia action, GC responsibility and success measure. Correct the summary together.

questions.text: What is the next real order we could start with, and what would you need before proceeding?
questions.hint: List/plan/quote needed, person responsible, due date, expected service scope and fee agreement. An interview is not approval to buy.

services.name: Takeoff & material cost check
services.when: Unclear quantities or the material portion of a subcontractor quote.
services.question: Who produces and verifies the list today, and which quantity or subcontractor inclusion was unclear on the last job?
services.action: Prepare or review quantities and estimated material costs for trade/GC approval.

services.name: Get supplier quotes
services.when: Time spent comparing suppliers or uncertainty about matching prices.
services.question: How did you compare the last quotes, including matching specifications, delivery and terms?
services.action: Compare like-for-like supplier quotes and negotiate approved material pricing.

services.name: Order through Avantia
services.when: Repeated supplier calls, payments or delivery arrangements.
services.question: Which supplier conversations, payments or arrangements did you personally handle on the last order?
services.action: Arrange approved purchases, supplier payments and delivery coordination.

services.name: Shortages & reorders
services.when: Missing items and repeated calls from subs.
services.question: Tell me about the last missing item: who identified it, approved it and arranged the reorder?
services.action: Receive a confirmed shortage list from the GC/sub and coordinate the approved reorder.
